evals.name: solution-shaped-ask-traced-to-the-need
evals.prompt: New backlog item ACME-301 from the sales managers: 'Add an Export to Excel button on the order list.' That's the whole ticket. Grill it so we can refine it.
assertions: Traces the 'Export to Excel' button back to the underlying need (what the sales managers do with the export) instead of accepting the button as the goal
Asks for or proposes explicit out-of-scope items
Does not grill or decide architecture or implementation (file-format library, endpoint, streaming, sync vs async download, query shape)
Has an explicit goal statement naming the user outcome rather than the Excel button (a story title may name Excel once the grilling has established it as the user's need)

evals.name: acceptance-criteria-that-cant-fail
evals.prompt: Ticket ACME-318: 'Customers get a reminder before their subscription renews.' Acceptance criteria: (1) Reminders work correctly. (2) The reminder is user-friendly. (3) Errors are handled gracefully. Grill the feature before we take it to architecture.
assertions: Flags all three acceptance criteria as uncheckable (they cannot fail)
Proposes replacement criteria that are observable pass/fail (e.g. when the reminder arrives, through which channel, what it says)
Probes edge-case scenarios around the reminder (e.g. cancelled before renewal, renewal date changes, no contact details)
Does not grill or decide implementation (scheduler, background job, email provider, retry policy)
Every drafted acceptance criterion is observable by the customer or an operator, none checks internal state (job status, stored flags)

evals.name: ask-term-conflicts-with-glossary
evals.prompt: Our CONTEXT.md defines **Customer** as the company that signs the contract and **User** as a person who logs in on a Customer's behalf; it says to avoid 'account'. Stakeholder ask ACME-325: 'When an account is suspended, all its users should be logged out and the account owner gets an email.' Grill the feature.
assertions: Calls out 'account' as conflicting with the glossary (Customer vs User) and asks which is meant
Challenges 'account owner' as a term missing from the glossary and proposes a canonical term
Proposes or records a glossary update rather than silently adopting the stakeholder's wording
The first message (section A) grills the terminology, not only the problem
Does not add scope the stakeholder didn't ask for (e.g. revoking API tokens, a reinstatement email) without raising it as a stakeholder question or listing it as out of scope

evals.name: product-decision-the-user-cant-make
evals.prompt: Grilling ACME-340 ('Let warehouse staff split a shipment into several parcels'). I don't know whether a split shipment should be invoiced once or per parcel — that's for the finance lead, who's out this week. Let's keep going on the rest.
assertions: Records the invoicing question as an open stakeholder question with a recommended answer
Does not settle the invoicing question on the user's behalf
Keeps grilling other parts of the feature in the same turn
Writes acceptance criteria, and every one that depends on the invoicing question is marked provisional and names the open question
Does not draft or offer an ADR

evals.name: stories-sliced-by-layer
evals.prompt: Scope for ACME-390 ('Customers can pause their subscription for up to three months') is settled. My draft split: (1) Pause API endpoint, (2) Pause button in the customer portal, (3) Database column for the paused state, (4) Billing skips paused subscriptions. Grill the split.
assertions: Flags the draft stories as sliced by layer or technology (API, button, database column)
Proposes a re-cut into stories that each deliver user-observable value end to end
Every drafted acceptance criterion is observable by the customer or an operator, none checks internal state (stored fields, flags, computed dates)
Does not grill or decide architecture (endpoint design, schema, data model) while re-cutting
Does not draft or offer an ADR
Drafts the story split onto the feature ticket and does not create or offer to create story tickets before grill-architecture has settled the split

evals.name: one-story-holds-the-whole-feature
evals.prompt: ACME-395 ('Warehouse staff can return damaged items to the supplier') — I've written it as a single story with these acceptance criteria: staff can register a return; the supplier gets a return notice; the item leaves stock; a credit note is booked when the supplier confirms; staff can see all open returns. Grill it.
assertions: Identifies that the single story holds several separately acceptable outcomes
Splits it into stories by outcome a user can accept, not by department, team or system area
Gives each proposed story its own acceptance criteria
States the order or dependencies between the proposed stories
Keeps open stakeholder questions separate from parked technical questions
Drafts the story split onto the feature ticket and does not create or offer to create story tickets before grill-architecture has settled the split

evals.name: criterion-restates-the-story
evals.prompt: Story under ACME-360: 'Sales reps can filter the order list by delivery region.' Acceptance criteria: (1) Sales reps can filter the order list by delivery region. (2) The filter is fast. Grill the story.
assertions: Flags criterion (1) as restating the story instead of saying how to check it
Flags 'the filter is fast' as uncheckable and asks for or proposes a measurable threshold
Proposes criteria covering all three of: only orders for the chosen region are shown; orders with no region; clearing the filter
Has an explicit out-of-scope list
Does not prescribe performance mechanics (index, cache, query shape) to make the filter fast
